![Threat Monitor screensaver](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kuydigital/threat_monitor/main/docs/screens.png)

**Storms explained in plain words.** Tropical cyclone alerts used to read like "Green tropical cyclone In-Fa". They now say what the storm is, where it is and how dangerous it is, for example "Typhoon In-Fa near the Marshall Islands, winds up to 241 km/h, low risk" or "Cyclone Arnab near India, 6 million people in winds over 120 km/h". Storms are called a typhoon, cyclone or hurricane depending on the ocean (or a tropical storm or depression when weaker), and GDACS's Green, Orange and Red levels are shown as low, medium and high risk. Earthquake alerts that said "2 thousand in 100km" now say "2 thousand people within 100 km". Created and maintained by Oliver Kuy.

Install the same way as before: on Windows, unzip and double-click **install.bat**; on a Mac, double-click **Threat Monitor.saver**. On a Raspberry Pi, run the one-line installer again to update. If you're updating on a Mac, log out and back in afterwards so macOS loads the new version.
